title: Whoa! 'The Odyssey' Sails Past $1 Billion at the Box Office—And It's Not Done Yet!
summary: Have you ever read a book so old it's almost 3,000 years old? Now imagine turning that ancient poem into a mega-hit movie! That's exactly what director Christopher Nolan did with 'The Odyssey,' and it's breaking records like crazy. In just three weeks, the movie has earned over $1 billion worldwide—that's $1,000,000,000! It's the first Nolan film to reach that milestone since 2012's 'The Dark Knight Rises.' The movie stars Matt Damon as Odysseus, a Greek king on a wild adventure filled with monsters, magic, and mayhem. Even though it's nearly three hours long and based on a really old story, audiences can't get enough. In the U.S. and Canada, it's made about $429 million, and internationally it's pulled in $578 million. A huge chunk of that—$257 million—came from IMAX screens, where the epic battles and stormy seas look absolutely jaw-dropping. Soon, 'The Odyssey' will become Nolan's highest-grossing movie ever, passing 'The Dark Knight Rises' ($1.08 billion). And here's the kicker: it hasn't even opened in China yet! China is the second-biggest movie market in the world, and it's rolling out the red carpet for the film on August 14, with nearly 800 IMAX screens ready. With all the buzz, experts think it will keep packing theaters all summer. This is the fifth movie of 2026 to join the billion-dollar club, following 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day,' 'Toy Story 5,' 'The Super Mario Galaxy Movie,' and 'Michael.' That's a huge deal—before this year, no year since the pandemic had more than three billion-dollar movies. Hollywood is hoping 'The Odyssey' and other blockbusters will push total ticket sales in North America past $4 billion for only the second time since COVID. So if you love big-screen adventures, grab your popcorn—this ancient tale is making modern history!
why_it_matters: It shows that stories written thousands of years ago can still pack theaters full of kids and adults, and maybe you'll want to explore the original tale yourself.

background_read: 'The Odyssey' is a very long poem written by the Greek storyteller Homer about 2,700 years ago, and it's one of the oldest adventure stories ever told.
Director Christopher Nolan (who made mind-bending movies like Inception and The Dark Knight) is famous for turning big ideas into huge movie spectacles.
When a movie earns more than $1 billion, it means millions of families around the world bought tickets, proving that a really old story can still feel brand new today.
Article_Structure: WHO: Director Christopher Nolan, actor Matt Damon, and the many people going to see 'The Odyssey' in theaters worldwide.
WHAT: The movie has crossed the giant milestone of $1 billion in ticket sales in just three weeks and is about to become Nolan's biggest hit ever.
WHERE: In the U.S., Canada, and many other countries, with a big opening in China still to come.
WHY: Audiences love the epic adventure on huge IMAX screens, and ancient stories still thrill people when told with amazing effects.

perspectives.description: It's a thrilling comeback for big-screen experiences, proving that people still want to see grand adventures in a dark theater with booming sound.
The three-hour runtime might be tough for younger kids, but the positive buzz shows that many families are making it a shared outing.
A box office smash based on Homer's poem introduces a whole new generation to one of the foundations of Western literature.
